clue.text: Attempts by Hazlitt, perhaps

definitions.meaning: tries or endeavours, the old sense of the word
William Hazlitt wrote short prose pieces of this kind, such as Table-Talk

explanation.definitionFit: The French essai means a trial, and Hazlitt is a master of the short literary prose form.

clue.text: Holy man (single) becomes novelist

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
one means single

explanation.surface: A celibate holy man turns his hand to writing fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Novelists of this name include Robert and Irving; 'becomes' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Stone and Irving Stone are both American writers of fiction.

clue.text: A sequel from Allen

definitions.meaning: a consequence or something that follows on
James Lane Allen wrote a novel of this title, itself a continuation of A Kentucky Cardinal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means consequences following an event, and Allen's 1896 book followed his earlier novel.

clue.text: Meredith heroine is an academician following a friend of Chopin

indicators.note: the academician comes after, following the friend in the answer

parts.note: George Sand, the novelist, was Chopin's companion
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel's heroine is described as an artist trailing in the wake of Chopin's companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra Belloni is the title heroine of George Meredith's novel of that name.

clue.text: Lear's botany was such rubbish

definitions.meaning: Edward Lear drew comic imaginary plants under the heading ... Botany

explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's invented plants appeared as his Nonsense Botany, and the word also means foolish talk.

clue.text: He rang baronet by arrangement, revealing satire on the Gothic novel

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the preceding letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A man rings a titled gentleman, and the call exposes a send-up of horror fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like the start of 'by arrangement', but it is part of the fodder; 'arrangement' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel mocks the vogue for Gothic romances such as Mrs Radcliffe's.

clue.text: Our Man in Italy, say, from Conrad

definitions.meaning: in Italian nostro uomo means our man, which the title character's nickname echoes
Joseph Conrad wrote a novel of this title

explanation.definitionFit: Conrad's title hero is nicknamed from the Italian for our man, and the book bears that name.

clue.text: Horseplay

parts.note: read as a play about horses, Peter Shaffer's drama about a boy who blinds horses

explanation.definitionFit: Peter Shaffer's drama about a stable boy takes its Latin title from the word for horse.

clue.text: Incorporeal adventures of Symons

definitions.meaning: without bodily substance, of the soul
Arthur Symons published a book of stories called ... Adventures

explanation.definitionFit: Something without a body belongs to the realm of soul, and Symons titled his 1905 stories this way.

clue.text: Stronghold gets fashionable supports from Shakespearian king

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold
in means fashionable
bras are supporting undergarments

explanation.surface: A fortress is equipped with stylish underwear by a royal character from the Bard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norwegian prince arrives at the end of Hamlet to take the Danish throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The young Norwegian prince in Hamlet claims the crown of Denmark in the final scene.

clue.text: "And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the and the Thummim exodus"

definitions.text: "And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the and the Thummim exodus"

parts.words: "And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the and the Thummim exodus"
parts.note: a quotation from Exodus 28:30 with one word missing, the object paired with Thummim

explanation.walkthrough: The verse in Exodus has a gap before 'and the Thummim'; the missing word fills it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus the high priest's breastplate holds two sacred lots, named together as a pair.

clue.text: Sort of pert and waggish poet

indicators.note: a sort of pert means the letters of that word put into some other order

parts.note: arch means playfully mischievous

explanation.surface: A versifier is described as somewhat cheeky and playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourteenth-century Italian wrote the sonnets to Laura.

clue.text: Art critic indicates the right American relative

parts.note: kin means a relative

explanation.surface: A critic of painting points out the correct relation from across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin was the great Victorian writer on painting and architecture.

clue.text: Drayton's notion of verse

parts.note: Michael Drayton titled his sonnet sequence with a word meaning notion

explanation.definitionFit: Michael Drayton's sonnet sequence carries a one-word title meaning a thought.

clue.text: Late talk recorded by King and Lyttleton

definitions.text: Late talk recorded by King and Lyttleton

parts.words: Late talk recorded by King and Lyttleton
parts.note: talk among the late, that is the dead: William King and Lord Lyttelton both wrote ... of the Dead

explanation.definitionFit: Conversations written as exchanges between speakers, here between the dead, form the genre both writers used.

clue.text: Flower seen where Aeneas lies buried

definitions.text: Flower seen where Aeneas lies buried

parts.words: Flower seen where Aeneas lies buried
parts.note: a flower is a river, something that flows; Aeneas was said to be buried by this river in Latium

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's river, a thing that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman legend placed the tomb of Aeneas on the banks of this small Latin river.

clue.text: Old king with sad dirge for poet

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: sad here means in a sorry state, so the letters of dirge are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aged monarch sings a mournful lament for a dead versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Is a beautiful French woman Dumas' eponymous queen?

parts.note: taken as written
belle is French for a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A question whether a lovely Frenchwoman is the royal title character in a Dumas work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumas wrote Isabel of Bavaria, named after the French queen consort.

clue.text: Matches I used in abstract art

indicators.note: the letters are used up and reworked in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone employs matchsticks in a non-figurative artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A French style of painting in blobs and splashes of colour, related to abstract expressionism.

clue.text: His early work anatomized wit

parts.note: this Elizabethan writer's first book was subtitled The Anatomy of Wit

explanation.definitionFit: John Lyly's Euphues: The Anatomy of Wit gave English the word euphuism.

clue.text: St Petersburg boy known as woodworker

definitions.meaning: Mark Twain's Tom lives in the Missouri town of St Petersburg

explanation.definitionFit: Twain's boy hero Tom lives in fictional St Petersburg, and a timber cutter takes the same name.

clue.text: Snare employed by Titania

definitions.meaning: one of the fairies serving Titania in A Midsummer Night's Dream bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: A spider's net traps insects, and the name belongs to a fairy in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: One of Hailey's well-rounded revolutionaries

parts.note: One such round thing revolves

explanation.definitionFit: A round object that turns on an axle, one of the plural in Arthur Hailey's motor-industry novel.

clue.text: Several characters recast as ragman

indicators.note: recast means formed again in a new shape

explanation.surface: Several figures are reworked as a rag-and-bone dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes letters rearranged, and the fodder demonstrates exactly that word game.

clue.text: Determined walk of little woman

definitions.meaning: the four sisters of Little Women share this surname

explanation.definitionFit: A purposeful stride, and the surname of Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy in Alcott's novel.

clue.text: His agnomen was by no means clear

definitions.text: His agnomen was by no means clear

parts.words: His agnomen was by no means clear
parts.note: an agnomen is an added nickname; Hardy's hero is called the Obscure, which means far from clear

explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's novel Jude the Obscure gives its hero an epithet meaning unclear.

clue.text: Petipa's ballet dancer

definitions.meaning: Marius Petipa choreographed the 1877 ballet of this name
the French term for an Indian temple dancing girl, with its article

explanation.definitionFit: Petipa's ballet is named after its heroine, a temple dancing girl in India.

clue.text: Instrument of false spy alert

indicators.note: a false alert is misleading, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A bogus warning about a secret agent sets off a musical sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient stringed instrument plucked like a zither.

clue.text: Concerning sound return from Hoffman's work

parts.note: re means concerning
an echo is a sound coming back

explanation.surface: A remark about sounds returning from a writer's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo again is to send a sound back, a repeated reverberation.
